Somerville.narrative: Somerville's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median of $1,245,000 and selling at 103.6% of list price — nearly two-thirds of them closing above asking. Condos, the most active segment with 51 sales in the past 30 days, are moving at exactly list price with a $787,000 median, while multi-families are the priciest play at $1,455,000 median with over half selling above ask at 101.4% SP/LP. With effectively zero months of supply across the board, this is an extreme seller's market where inventory is essentially nonexistent and well-priced properties are generating immediate, multiple-offer competition. Buyers should expect to move fast, come in above list with strong terms, and have financing buttoned up — while sellers who price strategically are consistently walking away with premium results.

Cambridge.narrative: Cambridge remains one of the most fiercely competitive markets in Greater Boston, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $2,490,000 and selling at 103.1% of list price — a striking 63.6% of those homes closing above asking. Condos, while more accessible at a $1,085,500 median, still saw 43.1% of units sell over list, and multi-families averaged $2,175,000 with 60% trading above ask, underscoring demand across every property type. With effectively zero months of supply across all categories and 104 total sales in the past 30 days, inventory is being absorbed as fast as it hits the market. For sellers, Cambridge is about as favorable an environment as exists — pricing aggressively is rewarded — while buyers should expect waived contingencies, escalation clauses, and the need to move decisively with strong pre-approvals in hand.

Milton.narrative: Milton's single-family market is firing on all cylinders, with a median sale price of $1,015,000 and a remarkable 59.1% of homes selling over asking price at an average of 104.2% of list price — clear evidence that buyers are competing hard for the town's limited inventory. With no calculable months of supply across all property types and 22 single-family homes closing in the past 30 days, demand is dramatically outpacing what sellers are bringing to market. The condo segment, while quieter with just 3 sales at a $595,000 median and a 99.3% SP/LP ratio, offers buyers a comparatively calmer entry point into this desirable South Shore community. For sellers, Milton represents an exceptional opportunity to command premium pricing, while buyers should come prepared with strong offers, flexible terms, and the expectation of multiple-offer situations — particularly in the single-family space.

Quincy.narrative: Quincy's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $745,000 and an eye-catching 102.8% sale-to-list ratio — nearly two-thirds of those 28 homes sold in the last 30 days went above asking price. Condos are moving briskly at a $550,000 median with all 29 units selling right at list price, while multi-family properties commanded a hefty $920,500 median with half of the 10 sales closing over ask. With essentially no months of supply across all categories, inventory is critically tight, giving sellers exceptional leverage and the confidence to price aggressively. Buyers should expect to compete hard, come in with strong offers above list — particularly on single-family homes — and have financing buttoned up before stepping foot through a door.

Watertown.narrative: Watertown's real estate market is firing on all cylinders across every property type, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $1,692,500 and a striking 75% of homes selling above asking price — a clear signal that inventory is critically tight with no measurable months of supply. Condos are the most active segment with 31 sales in the past 30 days at a median of $780,000, and while the 35.5% over-ask rate is comparatively modest, a 99.1% sale-to-list ratio confirms buyers are still paying close to full price. Multi-families are equally competitive, with 60% selling over ask and a median of $1,100,000, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant demand for income-producing properties in this well-located suburb. For sellers, this is about as favorable a market as it gets — properly priced homes are moving quickly and generating multiple offers — while buyers should arrive pre-approved, expect to waive contingencies, and be prepared to act decisively the moment a listing hits the market.

Medford.narrative: Medford's real estate market is firing on all cylinders, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $865,500 and a remarkable 60% of properties selling above asking price at an average of 100.4% of list price — a clear signal of intense buyer competition. Condos and multi-families are equally tight, with median prices of $765,000 and $1,200,000 respectively, and half of all listings in both categories closing over ask. With effectively zero months of supply across all property types and 58 total transactions closed in the past 30 days, inventory is critically scarce, giving sellers exceptional leverage to price confidently and expect multiple offers with minimal concessions. Buyers should be prepared to move quickly, come in strong above list price, and have financing locked in advance, as hesitation in this market almost certainly means losing out.

Melrose.narrative: Melrose's real estate market is firing on all cylinders, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,033,500 and sellers collecting an average of 103.6% of list price — nearly two-thirds of those homes (65.6%) selling above asking. The multi-family segment is even more aggressive, with the one sale recorded in the past 30 days closing at a striking 111.9% of list price and $1,175,000, signaling that investor demand remains fierce. With effectively zero months of supply across all property types, inventory is essentially nonexistent, meaning buyers must come prepared with strong pre-approvals, flexible terms, and the expectation of a competitive bidding situation. For sellers, conditions couldn't be more favorable — properly priced homes in Melrose are moving quickly and leaving money on the table for those who price strategically.

Arlington.narrative: Arlington's single-family market is firing on all cylinders, with a median sale price of $1,295,000 and homes selling at 107.3% of list price — nearly 80% of the 34 homes sold in the past 30 days closed above asking. The condo segment is somewhat more measured at a $817,500 median, with 27.8% of the 18 units sold fetching above list and an average sale-to-list ratio of 98.5%, though that still reflects healthy demand. Months of supply data is effectively zero across both property types, signaling an extremely thin inventory environment with far more buyers than available homes. For sellers, conditions are about as favorable as it gets — especially for single-family owners who can expect strong competition and premium offers — while buyers should come prepared with aggressive terms, pre-approval in hand, and realistic expectations about bidding wars in virtually every price range.

Belmont.narrative: Belmont's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with virtually no available inventory creating an acute supply-demand imbalance. Single-family homes are commanding a median of $1,975,000 with 61.5% of properties selling above list price and an average sale-to-list ratio of 101.3%, meaning sellers are consistently walking away with more than they asked — buyers should expect to bring their strongest offers and waive contingencies to compete. Condos are the most aggressive segment, with 77.8% selling over asking at a 104.8% sale-to-list ratio and a median of $850,000, signaling that even the entry-level Belmont market offers little relief for buyers hoping to negotiate. Multi-families at a $1,230,000 median are slightly more measured at 98.5% sale-to-list, but with only five sales in the past 30 days and no measurable months of supply, sellers across all categories hold overwhelming leverage in this market.

Winchester.narrative: Winchester's single-family market is operating at full throttle, with a median sale price of $2,400,000 and homes closing exactly at list price on average — though 44% of transactions are actually sailing over asking, a clear sign that well-priced properties are drawing competitive offers. With essentially no measurable months of supply and 25 homes sold in the past 30 days, inventory is being absorbed as fast as it hits the market. The condo segment is even more aggressive, with a median sale price of $1,015,000, 75% of units closing above list, and a sale-to-list ratio of 102.9%, suggesting buyers are routinely waiving contingencies and stretching budgets to secure a foothold in this desirable suburb. For sellers, Winchester represents one of Greater Boston's strongest positioning opportunities right now — accurate pricing will attract multiple offers quickly — while buyers should expect to move decisively, come in with clean terms, and be prepared to bid meaningfully above asking price in both segments.

Boston.narrative: Boston's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a $915,000 median sale price and a remarkable 102.1% sale-to-list ratio — meaning buyers are routinely paying above asking, with 60.7% of single-family sales closing over list price in just the last 30 days. The condo market, Boston's most active segment with 414 sales in the past month, sits at an $817,000 median while still seeing nearly 1 in 4 units sell above asking, and multi-family properties command a $1,200,000 median with 39% selling over list — reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant demand for income-producing assets. With essentially no measurable months of supply across all three categories, sellers hold enormous leverage and can realistically expect near-full or above-ask offers with limited concessions. Buyers should come prepared with pre-approval in hand, escalation clauses at the ready, and a willingness to move quickly, as hesitation in this environment almost certainly means losing out.
